children: BofA CLIENTS KEEP SELLING STOCKS, BUYING ETFs
BofA clients remained sellers of US equities last week, with the S&P 500

According to BofA Securities strategist Jill Carey Hall, clients were net sellers of US stocks for a second straight week. The selling was concentrated in individual stocks, which saw $11 billion of outflows, the third-largest weekly withdrawal in BofA's data dating back to 2008. At the same time, clients continued to put money into equity ETFs, adding $3.2 billion and extending that buying streak to 15 consecutive weeks.

Institutions were the primary sellers for a second week running. In contrast, both hedge funds and retail investors were net buyers, with retail posting its first inflows since late July. Clients sold individual stocks across all market-cap segments, though ETF demand was strong enough to leave small caps as a net beneficiary overall.

Corporate buyback activity picked up last week and remained slightly above seasonal norms. Still, year-to-date buybacks are tracking below 2024 and 2025 levels, while rolling 52-week buybacks as a share of S&P 500 market capitalization are at their lowest since August 2021.

Clients sold stocks in 9 of the 11 S&P sectors, with technology seeing the heaviest outflows, marking its fourth-largest weekly outflow in BofA's data dating back to 2008. Hall noted that the sector's four-week average flow has turned negative for the first time since mid-July. Communication services also posted sizable outflows.

Industrials registered their 10th consecutive week of outflows, the longest such streak since late 2023. Historically, Hall noted, similar stretches have often been followed by periods of relative underperformance versus the broader market.
Materials and real estate were the only sectors to attract fresh money.
On the ETF side, investors favored value and blend strategies, while trimming exposure to growth funds. Healthcare ETFs attracted the most buying, while technology ETFs saw the largest withdrawals.
Main US indexes red; Dow off most, down ~0.8%
Industrials weakest S&P 500 sector; just healthcare, staples positive
Dollar rallies; US crude dips; gold down >1%; bitcoin down >3%
